title: Repository Pattern
outcome: Introduce repository boundaries only where they improve persistence isolation, domain language, testing, or future changeability.
artifact: One TaskFlow aggregate/use case refactored behind a purposeful repository interface with real database integration tests.
labSteps: Choose a service whose persistence queries are complex enough to justify a boundary.
Write repository methods in application language rather than generic findAll/create/update/delete.
Move Prisma-specific selection/query details into the implementation.
Decide whether persistence types may cross the boundary or need mapping and document the trade-off.
Unit-test service behavior with a fake only where it proves useful behavior.
Integration-test the real repository against PostgreSQL so fake and implementation do not drift.
failureModes: Repository wrapping every trivial Prisma call with no value
Mocks proving an imaginary database behavior
Mapping everything into duplicate types without a domain need
mastery: Can explain when not to use a repository
Can test both service and real persistence
principles: Introduce a repository only when separating persistence behavior creates a real testing or architecture benefit.
A repository should express persistence operations in application terms rather than mirror every ORM method.
Keep Prisma-specific details from leaking through layers if the repository is intended to create a meaningful boundary.
Do not add repository abstractions to trivial CRUD solely because the pattern exists.
